production_direct.decision: Keep the plan pin. v1.62.0 was published 2026-11-07T09:13Z (hours before this lock): same SQLite 3.54.1, re-vendored lib/, libc bumped to v1.80.1, opt-in fdatasync (irrelevant: D1 runs synchronous=OFF), illumos port, Limit() through wrapped connectors (unused). Nothing we need; a same-day release with a libc bump is fresh risk. v1.61.1 carries the per-connection authorizer (v1.61.0) and the fixes for context-aware Rows.Next/Close and Tx.Commit waits.

Upgrade from the plan's v0.5.2. v0.5.3 is strictly stricter where we decode untrusted bytes: Decoder.Close streams and validates the page index against the decoded pages (count and page-number sequence) instead of io.ReadAll of the tail, rejects any byte after the trailer, and checks the index size field; Encoder aborts on any partial write instead of allowing a structurally incomplete file; compactor inputs no longer build page-index maps. Format bytes are unchanged for our range: the only checksum change excludes the SQLite lock page (pgno 262145 at 4 KiB pages, i.e. beyond the 1 GiB PENDING_BYTE), unreachable under the 256 MiB ceiling. Its encoder.go blob equals the main-branch encoder the plan inspected [S12]. Same go.mod and LZ4 dependency as v0.5.2.
Latest release, pinned together with the core module of the same SDK release commit.
Pinned with service/s3 from the same release commit. Currently '// indirect' in go.mod because no package imports it yet; the S3 adapter (aws.String, retry config) will make it direct.

rustfs_fixture.finding: Under 32-way contention on one key RustFS resets the TCP connection of some losing conditional PUTs (client: read: connection reset by peer, 7-115 ms) instead of delivering their 412: 3-13% of losers in some doctor races, 0 of 31000 losers in another 1000-round run, never a round's winner. Safe (the adapter classifies them Unknown and the library resolves them by reading), but a definite answer is lost; MinIO delivers every 412. The server waits for the full body before answering 412 and keeps connections usable after a 412 (raw-socket checks), so the cause is inside RustFS under load, not isolated further.

reusable_code_inventory: modernc.org/sqlite: database/sql driver, per-connection AuthorizerRegisterer via sql.Conn.Raw, sqlite_dbpage (ENABLE_DBPAGE_VTAB), context interrupts, Backup API for an independent snapshot oracle.
github.com/superfly/ltx v0.5.3: Encoder/Decoder (format 3, LZ4 blocks, CRC64 file checksum), ChecksumReader/ChecksumPage rolling database checksum, Compactor (AllowNonContiguousTXIDs=false).
aws-sdk-go-v2/service/s3: PutObject IfMatch/IfNoneMatch, GetObject IfNoneMatch, ListObjectsV2, DeleteObject; retryer must be overridden to one attempt for head writes.
No Litestream WAL-reader extraction: DECISIONS D2 replaces it with frame-header page numbers + sqlite_dbpage reads (proved by TestDBPageCapture).
m0_findings: Closing the last connection checkpoints committed-but-unpublished WAL frames into the main file even with wal_autocheckpoint=0 (TestCloseCheckpointsWAL), and modernc v1.61.1 exposes no SQLITE_DBCONFIG_NO_CKPT_ON_CLOSE. D2's 'close, delete -wal/-shm, reopen' discard is therefore unsafe; DECISIONS D10 makes discard delete the whole cache file and rehydrate.

The authorizer passes the table of CREATE TRIGGER/CREATE INDEX as arg2: the policy must test arg1 and arg2 against the reserved prefix, or an application trigger on a _state_ table would run inside library-mode statements. Views/triggers that read reserved tables are created but denied when used (TestAuthorizerPerConnection).
Authorizer mode switches must re-register the callback (expires prepared statements per modernc docs) rather than flip a variable read by a fixed callback.
Context deadline interrupts an unbounded recursive query in ~200 ms; the error satisfies errors.Is(context.DeadlineExceeded) and the pinned connection stays usable (TestContextInterruptsQuery).

D2 capture equals SQLite's own TRUNCATE checkpoint byte for byte across growth past 1000 pages, a spilled rolled-back transaction and VACUUM shrink; pages from rolled-back frames read back unchanged; pages above page_count are dropped (TestDBPageCapture).

ltx v0.5.3 accepts NoChecksum files at the codec level: the adapter must reject HeaderFlagNoChecksum itself. The compactor rejects TXID gaps but does not check pre/post checksum chains between inputs: the adapter must (TestLTXRejects).

ltx v0.5.3 DecodePage allocates the declared compressed frame size (up to 4 GiB) before reading it (TestLTXDeclaredSizeAllocation, 64 MiB shown): decode only bytes already matched to a head's SHA-256/length, and bound frame sizes before decoding untrusted input such as Import archives.
